data.description:
## Goal

Generalise the story-line content and authoring toolchain from `tce-main-street`
into core behind a **content adapter**, so any TCE game can author story-lines
through one validated, transactional seam. This is the prerequisite for the
visual editor and a child added during the migration to core (it did not exist
in the original `tce-main-street` plan).

## Context

The runtime engine already lives in core (`src/story-line/`). The authoring
seams it needs are still Main-Street-only and coupled to Main Street card
columns. Source implementations to generalise (read them, do not copy
Main-Street vocabulary into core):

- `tce-main-street` `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — `parseCsv`, `addCard`,
  `linkCard`, `applyToFile`, `parseAuthorArgs`; `applyToFile` writes atomically
  (temp file + rename) only after in-memory validation.
- `tce-main-street` `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — `validateStorylines`,
  `formatStorylineReport`, `storylineReportToJson`.
- `tce-main-street` `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — `buildStorylineManifest`,
  `serializeManifest`, `renderMermaid`, `filterManifestByStoryline`,
  `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`, `describeEventImpact`,
  `describeChoiceRouting`.
- `tce-main-street` `src/CsvChecksum.ts` — `computeCsvChecksum`.
- `tce-main-street` `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` — the manifest
  JSON schema shape.

Core facts: CLIs run under `tsx` (`npx tsx scripts/...`), not `vite-node`;
the module must stay Phaser-free and free of game imports; `ajv` is an existing
devDependency.

## Scope

- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — generic content model (`ContentCard`-like
  record) plus the **content adapter** seam: a game declares its CSV columns,
  the story-line field mapping (id, name, effect, choice flag, accept/reject or
  options encoding, storyline id/title) and any extra columns it wants editable.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — CSV parse/serialise against the adapter
  (column order preserved) and a content checksum for change detection.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — deterministic, timestamp-free manifest
  builder (nodes, edges, storyline ids/titles, cycles) plus Mermaid rendering and
  the per-storyline filtering/label helpers the viewer needs.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — validator over the compiled story-line
  model with a text report and a JSON report (cycles informational,
  `--fail-on-cycle` opt-in).
- `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — transactional author API: apply an edit
  in memory, validate, then write atomically; `--dry-run` and explicit content
  path supported; the **only** writer.
- Thin `tsx` CLIs over each seam: `scripts/storyline-author.ts`,
  `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` (with `--format mermaid|json --check`),
  `scripts/validate-storylines.ts`.
- A default adapter for the Gym demo content plus a fixture adapter used by
  tests, proving the seam is game-agnostic.
- A generic manifest JSON schema (e.g. `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json`)
  and `ajv` validation of generated manifests in tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A game-shaped fixture CSV round-trips byte-identically through
  `parseCsv` → `serialiseCsv` (column order preserved).
- The manifest builder produces the documented shape (nodes, edges, storyline
  ids/titles, cycles) and is deterministic: two runs are byte-identical and the
  `--check` mode reports drift only when the committed artefact differs.
- The validator catches at least: unknown successor id (dangling chain),
  duplicate card id, missing storyline id, and unreachable card; the text and
  JSON reports agree on the same findings, and an invalid input writes nothing.
- The author API refuses to write when validation fails, writes atomically on
  success, and `--dry-run` leaves the content file byte-identical.
- No core module in this change imports anything from a game repo or from
  Phaser; an import-boundary test asserts it.
- Unit tests cover the adapter seam with two different adapters (default Gym
  fixture + a second, differently shaped fixture).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `npm test` (unit projects) is green.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — **new** content model + adapter seam.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — **new** parse/serialise + checksum.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — **new** manifest + Mermaid.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — **new** validator + reports.
- `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — **new** transactional author API.
- `src/story-line/content/index.ts` — **new** barrel.
- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI.
- `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI with `--check`.
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **new** `tsx` CLI.
- `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` — **new** generic manifest schema.
- `tests/story-line/content/` — **new** adapter, CSV, manifest, validator and
  author tests.
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/` — **new** game-shaped fixture CSVs.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — **edit** authoring seams section.

## Deliverables

- Generic content model + adapter seam, CSV/checksum, manifest/Mermaid generator,
  validator, transactional author API, three `tsx` CLIs, manifest schema,
  parity/unit tests, documentation.
data.title: Storyline content and authoring toolchain generalised into core

data.description:
## Goal

Establish the shared test/verification foundation for the story-line editor so
every later core slice can be driven test-first. This task writes **test
infrastructure only** — no editor feature code.

## Context

Core test facts (verified):

- `npm test` runs `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` (unit → browser → tutorial E2E →
  Electron smoke). For implementation feedback use the cheaper profiles
  (`npm run test:dev`, `npm run test:smoke`).
- Vitest projects live in the root `vite.config.ts`: `unit` includes
  `tests/**/*.test.ts` (excluding `*.browser.test.ts`); `browser` runs
  `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` through `@vitest/browser-playwright` with
  chromium.
- `ajv` and `playwright` are existing devDependencies. Core CLIs run under
  `tsx`.
- `tests/story-line/helpers.ts` already provides an in-memory engine-adapter
  double — reuse and extend it rather than starting a second fixture style.
- Agent runs must go through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`);
  never invoke vitest directly.

## Scope

- Fixture helper that copies a content CSV plus generated manifest/Mermaid
  artefacts into an isolated temp directory and returns the paths, so edit tests
  never mutate committed files.
- A reusable write-path guard helper: scans editor source files and asserts no
  module writes a content CSV except through the core author module (tolerant of
  editor modules not existing yet).
- A manifest schema guard test (generated manifest validates against the generic
  schema with `ajv`) once `T0` lands; the guard must fail loudly if the schema
  path or artefact path moves.
- A browser-test harness decision/spike: determine and wire how a **non-Phaser,
  non-game** dev page is driven in the core `browser` project (or justify an
  alternative, e.g. a dedicated editor project), with a placeholder test that
  passes. Record the decision in a comment on this item.
- Paths in fixtures must derive from the generator's own exported defaults
  rather than hard-coded strings, so an artefact move fails one obvious test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture helper returns isolated temp copies of the content CSV and artefact
  files, and a test asserts the committed originals are byte-identical
  afterwards.
- The write-path guard is exercised by a test and would fail if an editor module
  wrote the content CSV directly (proven with a synthetic negative case).
- The generated manifest validates against the generic schema in a unit test
  using the existing `ajv` devDependency (or a documented, tracked skip until
  `T0` lands).
- The browser-test path for a non-Phaser dev page is decided, wired and
  documented; a placeholder browser test passes without adding a runtime
  dependency.
- The new harness is green under `npm run test:dev` and the core browser project.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `tests/story-line/editor/fixtures.ts` — **new** temp-copy helper.
- `tests/story-line/editor/fixtures.test.ts` — **new** helper test.
- `tests/story-line/editor/write-path-guard.ts` — **new** reusable static guard.
- `tests/story-line/editor/write-path-guard.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/story-line/editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` — **new** ajv guard.
- `./vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor/harness config (the root
  `vite.config.ts` stays the game/build config).
- `tests/story-line/editor/harness.browser.test.ts` — **new** placeholder wiring
  test.

## Deliverables

- Fixture helper, write-path guard helper, schema guard test, decided + wired
  browser-test path, harness smoke coverage.

data.description:
## Goal

A content designer can run `npm run storylines:editor` from the core repo root
and see a game's story-line graph rendered from the generated manifest, with
storyline grouping, choice-card distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom and node
selection. Read-only in this slice — no writes.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
understand an arc before changing it."

## Scope

- `scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — `tsx` entry point with `--help`, `--port`,
  `--host`, `--content <csv>` and `--adapter <module>`; boots the editor host and
  exits 0 on `--help`.
- Editor host serving the dev page via a dedicated `vite.editor.config.ts`
  (never the root `vite.config.ts`, which drives the game/Electron build).
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — pure mapper from the generic manifest
  (version/source/storylineIds/nodes/edges/cycles) to a render-ready view model
  (nodes, edges, storyline groups, choice flags, cycle flags), reusing the
  manifest module's `filterManifestByStoryline`, `nodeLabel`,
  `briefEventDescription`, `describeEventImpact` and `describeChoiceRouting`
  helpers rather than re-deriving them.
- `tools/storyline-editor/` — HTML page, app shell, and a lightweight SVG graph
  renderer (no new runtime dependency) with pan/zoom, node selection, storyline
  grouping, choice-card styling and cycle-edge marking.
- Sidebar/toolbar shell showing the selected node's links and metadata (name,
  effect, successor targets, storyline id/title, plus adapter-declared columns).
- Load one manifest and stay responsive at demo scale (no per-node network
  round-trip).
- `./package.json` — add the `storylines:editor` script.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run storylines:editor -- --help` exits 0 from the core repo root on the
  existing toolchain; no new runtime dependency is added.
- The editor loads a content CSV through the adapter and renders every node and
  edge of the generated manifest; choice cards are visually distinct, storyline
  grouping and cycle edges are shown, and pan/zoom plus node selection work.
- Selecting a node shows its links and metadata.
- A unit test diffs the view model (nodes, edges, storyline ids/titles, cycle
  flags) against the generated manifest and finds them identical.
- A browser test covers viewer rendering and node selection.
- No editor file is reachable from the production game entry graph
  (`./index.html` / `./main.ts`) or the Electron package; a build-exclusion
  assertion passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** entry point.
- `./vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor host config.
- `tools/storyline-editor/index.html` — **new** editor page.
- `tools/storyline-editor/app.ts` — **new** page shell.
- `tools/storyline-editor/graph-renderer.ts` — **new** SVG renderer.
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — **new** manifest view model.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — **reuse** manifest types and
  filtering/label helpers.
- `tests/story-line/editor/view-model.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/story-line/editor/viewer.browser.test.ts` — **new**.
- `./package.json` — **edit** add the `storylines:editor` script.

## Deliverables

- Launchable read-only editor, view model, SVG renderer, unit + browser tests,
  build-exclusion guard.

data.description:
## Goal

Edits from the editor are routed through the core transactional author API,
previewed and validated before writing, with committed artefacts regenerated and
a concurrency guard preventing lost updates.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want an edit to be previewed and validated before it
is written, so I cannot write a dangling chain or clobber someone else's edit."

## Scope

- `src/story-line/editor/api.ts` — thin bridge over the core seams, reusing their
  exported functions:
  - `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — edit application, `applyToFile`,
    storyline assignment via the card's storyline id/title fields (expose it as a
    single `setStoryline` wrapper for F4).
  - `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — validation + text/JSON reports.
  - `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — manifest build, serialise, Mermaid.
  - `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — content checksum.
  Expose `previewEdit`, `validateEdit`, `applyEdit`, `regenerateArtefacts`.
- Host API endpoints in `scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` (same toolchain as
  the CLI) for preview / validate / apply.
- Diff/preview response: before/after CSV rows for the affected card(s) plus the
  validation report.
- Concurrency guard: content checksum captured at load, compared before any
  write; on mismatch refuse and instruct a reload. Reuse the single checksum
  implementation from the content model — do not invent a second hash.
- All writes go through the author API, which writes atomically after in-memory
  validation; the bridge must not write the CSV itself.
- Artefact regeneration after an accepted edit: rewrite the committed Mermaid
  and JSON manifest artefacts and verify with `--check`.
- Hand-written doc sections are **not** machine-generated. When an edit touches a
  documented row, the bridge must return an explicit "manual documentation update
  required" result naming the check that now fails, instead of claiming the drift
  guard passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every edit returns a preview/diff and runs the validator before writing; an
  invalid edit exits non-zero, leaves the content CSV byte-identical, and
  surfaces the offending card/link.
- After an accepted edit the committed Mermaid/JSON manifest artefacts are
  regenerated and the `--check` drift guards report no drift.
- If the content CSV changed on disk since load, the bridge refuses to write and
  returns a reload instruction (unit test).
- No editor module writes a content CSV except through the core author API; the
  T1 write-path guard passes.
- A round-trip test on a fixture proves a valid edited fixture validates and,
  when the edit changes a hand-documented row, the bridge reports the required
  manual doc update naming the failing check.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/story-line/editor/api.ts` — **new** author/validator/manifest bridge.
- `scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` — **new** host API endpoints.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — **reuse** the content checksum.
- `tests/story-line/editor/bridge.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/story-line/editor/preview-validate.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/story-line/editor/concurrency.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Write bridge, host API endpoints, preview/diff payload, concurrency guard,
  artefact regeneration, unit tests.
data.title: Transactional write bridge and validation

data.description:
## Goal

Authors can edit existing card fields and add/relink a card through guided forms
that show a diff preview and inline validation before committing.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor links
in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a dangling
chain."

## Scope

- Edit form driven by the **content adapter's field descriptors** rather than
  hard-coded Main Street columns. Core-generic fields: id (read-only), name,
  effect text, choice flag, accept/reject successor links, storyline id and
  storyline title. Adapter-declared columns (e.g. Main Street coin/reputation
  deltas) render as additional typed fields without the editor knowing their
  semantics.
- Guided "add card" form that creates a card and links it into a storyline
  through the F2 bridge.
- Preview panel showing the pending diff; inline validation errors that block
  the write, rendered from the validator's text/JSON reports so the editor and
  the CLI report identically.
- Discard pending (unwritten) changes before committing, leaving the content CSV
  untouched.
- Wire the forms to the F2 bridge (`previewEdit` / `validateEdit` / `applyEdit`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The editor edits every core-generic field and every adapter-declared field; a
  round-trip test proves the edit validates and is written through the author
  API.
- The add-card form creates a card and links it into a storyline.
- Pending (unwritten) changes can be discarded before committing, leaving the
  content CSV byte-identical.
- A preview/diff is shown before each accepted edit; validation errors surface
  inline and block the write.
- A browser test drives a representative edit round-trip on a fixture.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `tools/storyline-editor/edit-forms.ts` — **new** adapter-driven field forms.
- `tools/storyline-editor/add-card-form.ts` — **new** guided add/link form.
- `tools/storyline-editor/preview-panel.ts` — **new** diff + validation panel.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — **reuse** the field-descriptor seam.
- `tests/story-line/editor/edit-forms.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/story-line/editor/edit-roundtrip.browser.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Adapter-driven card edit forms, add-card form, preview/diff panel,
  discard-changes support, unit + browser round-trip tests.
data.title: Curated card edit forms

data.description:
## Goal

Authors can create or rename a storyline group and reassign member cards through
the editor, driven through the same transactional author API (`setStoryline`,
exposed by F2 over the card's storyline id/title fields).

## Scope

- Storyline list view derived from the manifest's `storylineIds` and each node's
  storyline id/title, plus any group created in-session.
- Create a new storyline id/title group. A storyline exists implicitly through
  its member cards; there is no separate declaration file to edit.
- Rename an existing group and retitle it — a batch over every member card:
  apply the storyline fields to each member in memory, validate the combined
  result once before the first write, then write once through the author API.
- Reassign member cards to a group.
- All operations route through the F2 bridge and validate before write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a storyline group, renaming one, and reassigning member cards all
  route through the F2 `setStoryline` bridge and the validator before write.
- A batch rename writes exactly once (single author-API call), not once per
  member card.
- The storyline list reflects the regenerated manifest after an accepted edit.
- Tests cover create/rename/reassign against a fixture CSV without mutating the
  committed CSV.
- The T1 write-path guard still passes (no second CSV write path is introduced).

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `tools/storyline-editor/storyline-manager.ts` — **new** storyline CRUD UI.
- `src/story-line/editor/api.ts` — **reuse** the `setStoryline` bridge.
- `tests/story-line/editor/storyline-manager.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Storyline management UI, create/rename/reassign operations, unit tests.
data.title: Storyline management UI

data.description:
## Goal

Document the story-line authoring seams and the visual editor for content
designers and developers, and run the final full-suite regression sweep once all
editor features have landed.

## Context

- The core reference `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` currently documents the
  runtime module, the adapters and the Gym demo only; `T0` adds the authoring
  seams and this slice adds the editor.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` is the core tooling reference (scripts, test profiles,
  `npm test` = `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`); new `storylines:*` scripts must be
  discoverable there.
- Any generated artefacts (manifest/Mermaid, and any game-side generated docs)
  are produced by the `storylines:graph` CLIs; only hand-written prose may be
  edited, and `--check` must report no drift afterwards.
- Main Street keeps its own authoring docs and doc-drift guard; the change here
  is a note that its tooling now consumes the core seams, made in the
  `tce-main-street` repo (cross-repo per the core `AGENTS.md` rule).

## Scope

- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — authoring seams (content adapter, CSV,
  manifest, validator, author API) and the editor (launch, viewer, edit
  workflow, preview/validation, artefact regeneration, storyline management).
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — **new** developer/content-designer
  walkthrough, including how a game supplies its content adapter.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — list the new `storylines:*` scripts alongside the other
  tooling.
- Accurate doc comments on the new editor/authoring modules.
- `tce-main-street` — update its storyline authoring docs to note that the
  toolchain now lives in core (and keep its doc-drift guard green).
- Final full-suite regression sweep, including the Main Street storyline suites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the authoring seams and the editor
  (launch, viewer, edit workflow, validation, artefact regeneration).
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` documents how a game supplies a content adapter
  and how to run the editor against that game's content.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` lists the new `storylines:*` scripts.
- New editor/authoring modules carry accurate doc comments (no stale references
  to `vite-node` or main-street-only paths in core).
- `npm run storylines:graph -- --check` (and any game-side generated-doc
  `--check`) report no drift after any regeneration.
- The roadmap/seed reference to this work no longer lists the editor as
  deferred; it points at the shipped `npm run storylines:editor` tool.
- `npm test` in core passes (unit + browser + tutorial E2E + Electron smoke) and
  the `tce-main-street` storyline suites stay green; the story-line regression
  and parity harnesses stay green.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — **edit** authoring + editor sections.
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — **new** walkthrough.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — **edit** tooling list.
- `tests/story-line/` — **verify** stays green.
- `../tce-main-street/docs/game/storylines.md` — **edit** cross-repo note.

## Deliverables

- Updated core documentation, new editor walkthrough, accurate code comments,
  green full suite in both repos.
